title: ObjectFFRF: analytic Jacobian instead of the numerical one
author: Claude-JG
description: ObjectFFRF computes its ODE2 Jacobian numerically: one evaluation of the element per coordinate and a dense block of all coordinates. With the mass matrix as triplets (#2183) it is the largest cost of the element on larger meshes (7.9 s of 24 s for 1525 nodes and 20 steps). An analytic Jacobian - the stiffness and damping matrices as stored triplets plus the coupling terms of the floating frame, as for ObjectFFRFreducedOrder - returned as sparse triplets.
releaseNotes: ObjectFFRF computes its ODE2 Jacobian as sparse triplets - stiffness, damping and the quadratic velocity terms by the mesh coordinates analytic, by the rotation parameters by local differences -, on Euler parameters and Tait-Bryan angles without a forceUserFunction: 550 times faster than the numerical Jacobian at 1525 nodes; ObjectFFRF.numericalJacobian = True lets the system differentiate it as before
